title: AI in the design process

body.text: Claude doesn't replace the designer — it
speeds up the most time-consuming steps
— like writing briefs, brainstorming ideas, writing copy, and creating documentation, many times faster.

example: "Help me write a creative brief for rebranding a health app, target audience aged 25–40"

title: Design briefs with AI

body.text: the problem, the target audience, the goals, and the constraints
— tell Claude these, then have it help write a complete, clear brief.

example: "Write a design brief for a landing page selling an online course, target audience Thai freelancers aged 22–35"

question: Where does Claude help a designer best?

options.text: Speeding up briefs, copy, brainstorming, and documentation

question: What components should a design brief have?

options.text: The designer's name and the deadline only
The problem, target audience, goals, and constraints
No — Claude speeds up the work, but judgment and creativity still need a designer
Yes, but only for logo work

question: At which stages can you use AI in the design process?

options.text: It can't be used at all
From the brief and ideas, all the way to writing copy and documentation

question: How should you view AI in design work?

options.text: An assistant that helps think and speeds up work, not a replacement for design decisions
Something that does all the designing for you
